intended_object: The functor Cat.{v,u} ⥤ Cat.{max w v u, max w v u} that sends a category C to its universe-lifted copy `AsSmall C` (equivalent to C, but with objects and morphisms in a larger universe), and sends a functor F to the induced functor down ⋙ F ⋙ up. This is from the docstring.
explanation: On objects the definition gives `AsSmall C`, bundled as a category. On a functor F it gives `AsSmall.down ⋙ F ⋙ AsSmall.up`, which is the natural way to transport F to the lifted copies. Functoriality holds strictly, because `up` and `down` are inverse isomorphisms and composition of functors is associative. The `w` parameter lets the target universe be any level at least `max v u`, which is the most general choice. This is a universe-lifting construction, so no broader setting applies. I don't know of another Mathlib declaration that bundles `AsSmall` as a functor on `Cat`, so I give no counterpart.
